newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends lower on Central Bank's cue.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends lower on Central Bank's cue.

text.p: The Philippine peso closed fractionally lower at 26.299 to the U.S. dollar from Wednesday's 26.298 after the Central bank trended its dollar buying rate upward, traders said.

The peso opened stronger at 26.293 due to the absence of dollar demand and the continued inflow of portfolio money, one trader said. Another trader said some banks were trying to test the Central Bank on how high it would allow the peso to go.
However, when the peso reached 26.287, the Central Bank moved in and bought dollars. The Central Bank further nudged its rate upward up to 26.298 in late afternoon.
"From 26.287, the peso went down very quickly reaching the Central Bank's selling rate of 26.30," one trader said.
One trader estimated that the Central Bank bought about $20 to $30 million and sold about $5.0 million.
Traders expected the peso to weaken further on Friday as banks take advantage of the weekend swap points.
